/-!
# Erdős Problem 159

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/159](https://www.erdosproblems.com/159)
- [Er78] Erdős, P., Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory. Proc. Ninth Southeastern Conf. Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1978), 29-40.
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos159

/--
There exists some constant $c>0$ such that
$$R(C_4,K_n) \ll n^{2-c}.$$

The prize of $100 is offered in [Er78] for a proof or disproof.

This problem is #17 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_159 :
    ∃ (c : ℝ) (_ : 0 < c) (C : ℝ),
      ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n →
        (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)
          (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - c) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos159

reformulations.difference: Lean requires R(C₄,Kₙ) ≤ C n^(2-c) for every n ≥ 1, allowing a multiplicative constant C. The original source [Er78], Section 4, equation (5), instead requires R(C₄,Kₙ) < n^(2-ε) for all sufficiently large n, for some fixed ε > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An eventual bound without a prefactor extends to all positive n by enlarging C to cover the finitely many exceptions; every denominator n^(2-ε) is positive. Conversely, from Lean's bound choose ε = c/2. Eventually n^(c/2) > C, giving C n^(2-c) < n^(2-c/2). Both directions, and equivalence with the big-O formulation, were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The absence of an explicit positivity condition on C is harmless: a separate Lean proof establishes R(C₄,K₁)=1, so the n=1 inequality forces C ≥ 1.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory (1978), Section 4, pp. 33–34, especially equation (5): https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-36.pdf
review.notes: No mathematical mismatch found in the sole declaration. Checked non-induced graph containment, the Ramsey infimum, the square's adjacency and degree, real exponent semantics, quantifier scope, and boundary cases. Finite Ramsey theory ensures the defining infimum is over a nonempty set. Scratch proofs also establish R(C₄,K₀)=0 and R(C₄,K₁)=1; final compilation has no errors or warnings, and the equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx. Source-access limitations: erdosproblems.com/159 returned Cloudflare challenges, and Sp77's full text was inaccessible. The conjecture and historical $100 prize were verified directly in Er78. The supplementary public problem database records problem 159 as open, consistent with the file; the website's current remarks/status could not be checked directly.
